analysis.title: GS Quek - Weekend Thoughts 41/53: European stress, US 3Q, Differentiated Asia
key_insights: Global equities rose for another week despite worries over the Fed and rates path, European yields and contagion risk, oil headlines and a weakening consumer. Client conversations point to resilient US macro and earnings, but activity is lower as the market crowds into the same areas.
Global equities were net sold this week (net bought last week), led by US and EM Asia. US Tech was the most net sold US sector after being most net bought in 4 of the past 5 weeks.
The Software-to-Semis rotation continues: GSPUSOSE +12% for the week and +61% from June lows.
Gross/net allocations to US Tech recovered to the 87th/83rd percentile versus the past year. Mag7 positioning is at a record 22% of total US exposure, versus 14% in June.

Upcoming catalysts: CPI next Wednesday for rates, 3Q earnings for AI, and the midterms for geopolitics. GS expects the next Fed hike in December (pushed back from October), with a strong chance the FOMC concludes further tightening is unnecessary.

French 10-year bond spreads are at the highest level since 2012. GS does not expect a systemic crisis or broad earnings shock in Europe, as institutional backstops are stronger and the ECB could implement programs to stabilize bond markets if disorderly dynamics emerge.
Euro area FCI has tightened by about 40bp since July, which GS thinks could substitute for one 25bp ECB hike. GS still calls for a third and last ECB hike in December.

European equities are 5.7% off peak and have underperformed other regions. Mitigating factors: EPS upgrades across most sectors (ex-discretionary) since July, a 5.5% FCF yield, ongoing buybacks and negative net equity supply. GS likes Technology, Banks, Renewables (GSSBRNEW), Defense (GSSBDEFE) and Capital intensive (GSSTCAPI).

US 3Q earnings: 70% of SPX market cap reports by end of month, with most hyperscalers in the last week. The Street expects 27% YoY growth (33% in 2Q). GS expects the median stock to print 9% earnings growth versus 14% in the prior quarter.
GS equity analysts expect cloud revenue growth to accelerate from 48% in 2Q to 55% in 3Q. Given this and cloud backlog, GS thinks hyperscalers can generate more than 15% ROIC on AI capex.

Record equity issuance of $430bn YTD (double 2025) is a concern, and GS expects another $600bn in 2027. GS argues it is not out of line when scaled against market cap, and buyback authorizations are 20% higher YoY. 12m SPX target is 8700.

Under the historical playbook of SPX versus Fed hikes, US equities have bottomed 2-3 months after the first hike, which would roughly coincide with the midterms. Quek would take time here and keep dry powder for the post-event window.

HFs net sold Asia equities for a 4th consecutive month in September, led by Korea Tech, with marginal net buying in Taiwan. Net allocation to Asia is at the 68th/94th percentile on 1-year/5-year lookbacks, a 12.9% OW versus MSCI World AC (June peak 19.5%, 6.5% at start of year).
Asia Tech was the most net sold for the fourth straight month and has reversed all buying in more than a year. It is 19% of Global Net MV versus a 27% June peak and 10% at start of year.

Tim Moe's team argues the case for Asia is compelling over the medium and long term. Taiwan and Korea are now the top index markets, China's weight has more than halved from peak at 19%, and Tech is 43% of the index. GS expects regional earnings of +25%/+14% in 2027/2028 after +75% in 2026 and raised 10-year trend earnings growth to 10% from 9%.
Non-Tech Asia themes include corporate reforms, dividend plays, HALO and US reindustrialization. Korea's reform momentum is on track with about 70% of stocks trading below book.

October Conviction List additions: AMZN, BURL, HII, JCI, OXY, Solaria, Strauman, Scout24, IMCD, Panasonic, CATL, Zijin Mining, Weichai Power, Food & Life and Hanwha Aerospace. Next week's note covers Power Up, European Luxury and India banks.

tension_points.bull_case: Resilient US macro and earnings, cloud revenue growth accelerating to 55%, hyperscaler ROIC above 15%, buyback authorizations up 20% YoY, 12m SPX target 8700.
